spec.question: Can existing Microseed owners handle simultaneous non-comparable local and higher-order regulatory pressures without hidden scalarization or a central arbiter?
spec.incumbent: Scope, obligation, currentness, action qualification and hierarchical separation can yield lawful dominance or abstention without combining pressures into one scalar.
spec.rival: Observed conflict resolution requires an implicit weighted-sum/central arbitration mechanism.
spec.manipulation: Create a fixture with two simultaneously current regulatory pressures: action A satisfies only local viability, action B satisfies only higher-level requested effect, and action C abstains. Do not supply a combined utility. Repeat while multiplying/swapping numeric pressure magnitudes without changing hard scope/obligation relations.
spec.incumbent_prediction: When constraints are genuinely incompatible Microseed abstains/refuses rather than scalarizing; when one action satisfies all active hard constraints it is selected; magnitude rescaling alone does not flip a hard-constraint decision.
spec.rival_prediction: Choice flips predictably with pressure magnitude/weights even when hard authority/scope relations are unchanged, revealing scalar arbitration.
spec.measurement: Candidate set, rejection reasons, obligation/scope traces, selected/abstained action, sensitivity to magnitude rescaling.
spec.minimal_embodiment: Research-only action-selection/regulatory fixture using existing value/obligation owners.
spec.falsifier: Behavior requires or reveals a combined scalar/central policy to resolve the matched fixture.
spec.loop_plus: If no decision emerges, distinguish lawful incomparability from search/candidate-generation failure.
